note: Rewritten from Sands' (1999) new species description, original in English; the genus lacks soldiers, only the worker has a complete description; measurements follow the original ranges.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Differences from A. autothysius are given under that species: the fourth marginal tooth of the left mandible just touches the lateral edge of the molar prominence, the fore tibia is proportionally longer, and the enteric valve is six-radiate with large, straight conical spines. From A. congoensis it differs in that the latter has shorter legs, the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible as long as that of the first, the proximal end of the fourth marginal tooth not touching the molar prominence, the third lobe of the enteric valve seat nearly as large as the other two lobes, and the spines of the primary rows curved on the three-radiate valve. From A. cristatus it differs in that the latter has a smaller third distal spur of the fore tibia, the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible as long as that of the first, fewer apical spines in the primary rows, and far less developed secondary rows.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white or pale yellow, the darkest part of the antennal flagellum, the pronotum and the legs yellowish white, abdominal tergites transparent. Head capsule circular or short-oval, nearly circular, setae sparse, projecting, the longest setae arranged regularly and symmetrically. Fontanelle absent. Fore coxa without stout setae, or with 1—3 stout setae on the anterior surface; fore tibia with 3 distal spurs, the third well developed, at least one-half the length of the others. Left mandible: first marginal tooth nearly equilateral, anterior margin of the third marginal tooth shorter than that of the first marginal tooth, the fourth marginal tooth just touching the lateral edge of the molar prominence in frontal view; right mandible: anterior margin of the first marginal tooth equal to or shorter than that of the second marginal tooth. Measurements: head width 0.652—0.711 mm; pronotum width 0.411—0.468 mm, length 0.192—0.251 mm; hind tibia length 0.696—0.794 mm; fore tibia length 0.589—0.632 mm; left mandible index 0.731—0.902, right mandible index 0.992—1.187.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The midgut–hindgut junction arises ventrally to the left of the nerve cord or below it; the first hindgut segment is rather long, up to more than 8 times as long as its proximal width, tubular throughout or inflated to about 2 times the basal width; in the undissected abdomen the enteric valve lies to the right of the heart (dorsal view) or to the left of the nerve cord (ventral view); the third lobe of the enteric valve seat is smaller than the outer pair. The enteric valve ridges are nearly taper-ellipsoid from the base towards the apical spines, the ends weakly sclerotized, pale yellow or yellow; the primary rows of all ridges bear large, upright conical spines directed backwards, at most 10—20, the longest straight and evenly tapering, not wider than the narrowest point of ridge three, the symmetry nearly six-radiate except for slight differences in ridge size; the secondary rows consist of conspicuous spines covering the whole ridge surface, lengthening towards the ridge apex, the outlines of the scales or reticulation blurred; the membrane between and outside the ridges bears numerous but not dense minute spines, with marginal scales proximally.
